paper.title_en: The inner dark-matter structure of TNG50 simulated galaxies
paper.abstract_en: In the $Λ$CDM framework, galaxies evolve within dark matter (DM) haloes, where baryonic processes can modify the inner structure of the DM distribution. In particular, the condensation of baryons and associated feedback mechanisms can alter the inner density profiles of haloes, motivating detailed studies of their central regions. We investigate inner DM density slopes in TNG50 galaxies, their relation to galaxy properties, and their cosmic evolution. We assess baryonic effects on the inner DM structure by comparing galaxies with their DM-only (DMO) counterparts. We constructed spherically averaged DM density profiles in both runs. The inner slope was quantified using an inner linear fit, defined as a direct power-law fit to the central region of the density profiles and motivated by the asymptotic behaviour of generalised Navarro-Frenk-White models. Subhaloes were matched between simulations and tracked across redshifts $z = 0$, $0.2$, $0.7$, and $1$. The inner DM structure of galaxies in TNG50 shows that high-stellar-mass systems ($M_\star \gtrsim 10^{11}$ M$_\odot$) exhibit shallow inner slopes regardless of whether they are centrals or satellites, while lower-mass galaxies ($M_\star \lesssim 10^9$ M$_\odot$) show a broader diversity of profiles. At fixed stellar mass, low-mass satellites tend to be more cuspy, with the steepest slopes found in redder systems with lower $V_{\mathrm{max}}$ in more massive host haloes. At the population level, we find a modest cosmic evolution, with steeper profiles towards low redshifts in the hydrodynamical run and the opposite trend in DMO, while hydrodynamical galaxies remain systematically steeper at all redshifts. Finally, we verified that the fiducial interval provides the most suitable reference for measuring the shallowest inner slopes of DM density profiles at the TNG50 resolution limit.
